html:
SMTO-SKL-0122 — Your Slack connection doesn't have permission for this

GUID: 0cba7ddb-2e0c-5620-84c7-aa856ff6df7a
Slug: slack-scope-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • The Slack connection SMTO is using wasn't given the Slack permission this request needs, so it was refused. Nothing in Slack was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent which Slack permissions this request was missing, or look for them in the error details. Slack calls them scopes, for example chat:write or files:read. SMTO records which permissions were missing, so you add only what this request needs.
  2. Open Parameter Store, open your Slack OAuth App entry, add the missing permission to its requested scopes, and save. Add it to the app's settings on Slack's website too, if your app requires that. SMTO only asks Slack for the permissions listed in that entry.
  3. Ask the Agent to connect Slack again with the same workspace key, and approve the new permission on the Slack page. Slack only grants added permissions after you approve them again.
  4. Ask the Agent for your request again. The request was refused before anything changed, so it's safe to repeat once the permission is granted.

What success looks like

  • Asking the Agent to list your Slack workspaces shows the new permission, and the request completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your Slack workspace admin or the person who manages your Slack app. Don't connect a different Slack account just to get around the missing permission.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested Slack operation needs a scope that the selected slack_workspace profile's granted_scopes do not include, or Slack returned missing_scope.

What this means

  • Local method-scope checks fail or Slack reports missing_scope. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Local method-scope checks fail or Slack reports missing_scope.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect required_scopes and the exact operation's supported alternatives.

How to fix it

  • Read required_scopes in the error details; add them to requested_user_scopes or requested_bot_scopes in the Slack OAuth App profile (and to the Slack app's configuration), then run slack.connect again with the same workspace_key so the same principal grants them. SMTO never substitutes another token.
  • Review required_scopes and reconnect the same principal with the needed method scopes; never substitute another token automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended principal deliberately grants the required method access.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
